_doc: Text both sides render from one table (docs/API.md '언어·웹'): activity sentences (app feed, server push), push batch and reminder text, invite landing pages, category labels, frequency words and the money notation M(x). Keyed by language (en ko nl fr de id it ja pl pt es sv th); 'en' is the source and the fallback: a missing language renders 'en', a missing key or variant renders the 'en' one. Copies that must stay byte-equal: app/assets/strings.json, server/src/main/resources/strings.json. Templates use {placeholders} only (no ICU, no plurals): a value is inserted verbatim in one left-to-right pass, so a description containing '{A}' stays as typed. Every language has every key and variant of 'en' with the same placeholders. activity.<kind> variants: 'self' when the subject is the viewer, 'you' when the object is the viewer, else 'other' (a missing variant falls back to 'other'). A {name}-like placeholder can hold a member name, words.you or words.someone: don't attach affixes that only fit names (e.g. Korean 님) to placeholders that can hold words.you. words.you/words.someone at the very start of a sentence get their first letter upper-cased; member names never change. Batch sentences ({n}) must read correctly for every n >= 2. suffix.* is joined to a sentence with words.dot and also stands alone (the app's feed line). Not translated: member and group names, descriptions, comments, brand and provider names, currency codes, ISO dates in change lists. Phase 10: email.* (plain-text emails; the server adds the greeting, the '—' line and the footer), unsubscribe.* (the unsubscribe page), activity group_deleted/group_restored (friend_deleted/friend_restored: the same kinds in a friend group, whose name is internal), email.recurring.footerSelf (the reader made the series), changes.type/coverImageId, words.groupType (an unknown type reads as other).
